PyFixest 0.70 exposes fitted-model state through typed components. Private
attributes from 0.60 are not supported, except for the compatibility names
listed below. Accessing a removed private name raises an `AttributeError` with
a link to this guide. Some private names are still used internally; their
presence does not make them part of the supported API.

## Find the replacement

Use the component that owns the information your code needs:

| Information | Component or method |
|---|---|
| Formula, dependent variable and fixed effects | `fit.model` |
| Estimation options | `fit.options` |
| Supported operations (`_support_*`, `_supports_*`) | `fit.capabilities` |
| Observation counts and dropped rows | `fit.sample_info` |
| Fixed-effect counts (`_k_fe`, `_n_fe`) | `fit.fixef_counts` |
| Original model inputs | `fit.model_matrix` |
| Observation weights (`_weights`) | `fit.observation_weights` |
| Demeaned inputs for linear and IV models | `fit.within_data` |
| Within preconditioner (`_preconditioner`) | `fit.preconditioner` |
| GLM working values | `fit.working_state` |
| GLM convergence (`_convergence`) | `fit.convergence` |
| Quantile solver state (`_it`, `_x_final`, etc.) | `fit.solution` |
| Collinear regressors or instruments (`_collin_*`) | `fit.collinearity`, `fit.collinearity_instruments` |
| Coefficients, standard errors and confidence intervals | `fit.coeftable` |
| Covariance matrix and inference settings | `fit.variance_covariance` |
| Fit statistics and fitted values | `fit.fitstat`, `fit.fitted_values` |
| Sandwich components, when available | `fit.sandwich` |
| IV first stage and diagnostics | `fit.first_stage` |
| Wald test results (`_dfn`, `_dfd`, `_f_statistic`, etc.) | `fit.wald` |
| Randomization inference results (`_ritest_*`) | `fit.ritest_statistics` |
| Saturated event-study design (`_yname`, `_att`, etc.) | `fit.event_study_design` |
| Fixed-effect estimates (`_fixef_dict`) | `fit.fixef()`, `fit.fixef_estimates` |

Components differ between estimators, and some data may be unavailable when
storage options such as `lean=True` are used. Their shapes, weighting, and
contents may also differ from the 0.60 private attributes. See the [API
reference](/reference/index.qmd) for each component's contract. In particular,
`fit.resid()` returns response residuals; the old `_u_hat` on weighted linear
and IV fits was multiplied by the square root of the observation weights.
`fit.fixef_estimates` is available after calling `fit.fixef()`.

## Compatibility names

Names without a leading underscore and three documented IV names remain as
deprecated aliases or raise a specific removal message. Names read by released versions of
[marginaleffects](https://github.com/vincentarelbundock/pymarginaleffects) and
[maketables](https://github.com/py-econometrics/maketables) remain available
without a warning. These aliases can reflect estimation or inference changes
since 0.60; see the [changelog](/changelog.qmd).

After compatible releases of both packages use typed state, the plan is to turn
on warnings for their aliases. No removal version is scheduled yet.

Other retained aliases emit `PyfixestDeprecationWarning` (a `FutureWarning`).
To find their use in your test suite, turn the warning into an error:

```{python}
#| eval: false
import warnings
from pyfixest.errors import PyfixestDeprecationWarning

warnings.simplefilter("error", PyfixestDeprecationWarning)
```

With pytest, add `"error::pyfixest.errors.PyfixestDeprecationWarning"` to the
`filterwarnings` setting. Silent aliases do not emit a warning, while removed
names raise `AttributeError`.

The table lists the retained compatibility names. Entries for `Feols` also
apply to IV, GLM, and quantile models, unless a more specific entry is listed.

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
from pyfixest.estimation.models._deprecated_attributes import (
    DEPRECATED_ATTRIBUTES,
    Removed,
)

print("| Old attribute | Model classes | Use instead | Status |")
print("|---|---|---|---|")
for attribute in DEPRECATED_ATTRIBUTES:
    for class_name, entry in attribute.classes.items():
        status = f"removed: {entry.reason}" if isinstance(entry, Removed) else (
            "silent alias" if attribute.silent else "deprecated alias"
        )
        print(f"| `{attribute.name}` | `{class_name}` | `{entry.replacement}` | {status} |")
```
